## Warranty Policy
1-Year Warranty Assurance:
We offer a comprehensive one-year warranty starting from the date of purchase. Our warranty covers repairs caused by non-human factors, including manufacturing defects and functional issues under normal use. We also provide professional guidance and assistance for any product-related inquiries during the warranty period.
Please note that the warranty period complies with the applicable consumer protection laws in the country where the product is purchased.
Customer Service:
If you have any questions or need warranty support, please feel free to contact us:
📧 ks@cephalon.ai
Our team will be happy to assist you and ensure you have the best possible experience with Lucy AI Studio.
risks: Like any crowdfunding effort, this venture comes with its own set of risks and challenges that we want to be upfront about. Launching a new product inevitably involves a few surprises along the way. What makes Kickstarter special is that it invites backers to be part of that journey, offering an inside look at the realities of product development and production. Our extensive experience in production gives us strong confidence in our ability to navigate and resolve any unexpected issues that may arise during manufacturing. As we move through the final stages, we’re committed to keeping communication open and frequent, so you’ll always know where things stand. We’re truly grateful for your trust and patience as we take this path together, and we’re determined to deliver a final product that meets your expectations.

faq.q: Is LUCY supposed to have some form of a NAS UI or anything like a Ugreen or Synology NAS?
faq.a:
LUCY is not designed around a traditional NAS interface like the ones you'd find on Synology or Ugreen. The reason is that we see the NAS functionality as something that is primarily AI-driven, rather than something users have to manually manage through a conventional dashboard.

Instead of browsing folders and files yourself, you can interact with LUCY through a LUI (Language User Interface) and ask the AI to find and work with the information you need. For example, LUCY can search its indexed…

faq.q: Is it more designed just as a “do anything” box that comes with Linux pre-installed, but you could technically install Windows on it, or any distro of Linux that you’d want and that sort of thing?
faq.a:
LUCY is more than just a hardware box with Linux installed. We're building it as a complete AI Studio solution that combines hardware, software, AI agents, and workflows. The current system is Linux-based, and we’re also developing a more AI-native operating environment together with Lucy Harness, the Lucy app, and related workflows.

A useful way to think about it is something like a Mac Studio: the value isn't just the physical hardware, but the overall ecosystem and experience built around it…

faq.q: Where should I go to access the LUI and set up content indexing?
faq.a:
LUCY is an open AI computing box, meaning you can technically deploy any agent frameworks you like (including Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, etc.). However, we strongly recommend focusing your evaluation on Hermes.

The main reason—beyond workflow agility—is cost-efficiency and architecture:
Hybrid Local & Cloud Execution: Hermes supports auxiliary models and Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) setups. It routes heavy lifting or routing tasks locally while leveraging lightweight or cost-effective cloud model…

faq.q: The OS: Ubuntu Today → Highly Customized Omarchy (Lucy AIOS) at Launch ?
faq.a: Your current test unit runs on standard Ubuntu, not our final OS. We are in the process of transitioning to Lucy AIOS, which is built on a highly customized, agent-first version of Omarchy. Depending on production and shipping timelines, retail units will ship with this optimized Omarchy/Lucy AIOS environment rather than the generic Ubuntu setup you have now. Because both Omarchy and Hermes are deeply rooted in open-source foundations, they are being co-optimized to work seamlessly together out…

faq.q: What is the Lucy App / Lucy AIOS? (Roadmap vs. Today)
faq.a:
Neither the Lucy App nor the complete Lucy AIOS frontend experience are officially launched yet; both are actively under development.

To be completely transparent about what the Lucy App actually is:
The Lucy App is essentially a simplified, user-friendly remote client for Hermes. Think of it as a low-friction interface designed for mainstream users who don't want to deal with configuration.
